title: ProcessingJobResult v1
description: What one attempt produced (lai_processing.contracts.results.ProcessingJobResult). Processing success is not asset approval: status says whether the worker ran the job to the end, verdict what the processor concluded; neither publishes anything. Shared definitions live in job_request.v1.schema.json. The Python decoder is authoritative and also enforces cross-field rules: a succeeded result has a verdict and a processor and no errors; a pass verdict has no error findings; a failed or cancelled result has errors and no verdict; retry_class equals the first error's classification; error messages equal the fixed safe message of their code; artifacts belong to this job, attempt, namespace, profile and processor with unique logical ids.

attempt_id.description: The attempt that produced this result.

processor.description: The processor that ran; null only when no processor was resolved (a failure before dispatch).

profile.description: The profile version the attempt used.

status.description: Worker execution result: succeeded, failed or cancelled.

verdict.description: The processor's conclusion about the input for a succeeded result (pass, fail, not_applicable); null otherwise.

retry_class.description: Retry class of the primary (first) error; null for a success.

input.description: The input as the worker observed it, or null when it was never read.

started_at.description: When the attempt started (UTC, Z suffix).

completed_at.description: When the attempt finished; not before started_at.

duration_ms.description: Measured execution time in milliseconds (at most one day).

metadata.description: Processor-specific JSON metadata (bounded nesting, no NaN, string keys of at most 128 characters, canonical size at most 256 KiB and the job's max_metadata_bytes). Never input text or child data.

findings.description: Validation findings about the input (at most 500).

warnings.description: Notes about the processing run itself (at most 50).

errors.description: Classified errors (at most 8); empty for a success, non-empty otherwise.

artifacts.description: Immutable references to derived objects this attempt wrote.

retry_class.description: retryable (bounded automatic retry), permanent (never retried), cancelled, manual (operator action).

processor_identity.description: Which processor, and which release of it, produced a result or artifact.

processor_version.description: Semantic version of the processor release.

input_identity.description: The input as observed. verified is true only when the whole object was read and matched the request's size and SHA-256.

ref.description: The object read (with the version actually read when known).

verified.description: Whether size and checksum were verified against the request.

finding.description: One validation finding, in the Asset Library's finding shape.

message.description: Message authored by processor code, never input text (at most 500 characters).

path.description: Location inside the input the finding refers to, or empty (at most 200 characters).

warning.description: A note about the processing run (not about the input's validity).

job_error.description: A classified error. message is always the fixed safe text for code, and retry_class always the code's classification (core/errors.py).

message.description: The fixed safe message for code (SAFE_MESSAGES); anything else is refused.

details.description: Short scalar facts safe to persist and log (at most 16 entries; identifier-like keys of at most 64 characters; strings of at most 200 characters without newlines).

artifact_reference.description: A durable, immutable pointer to one derived object. Identified by store, key, version and checksum, never a presigned URL. Its key must sit under processing/artifacts/<namespace>/<source_job_id>/<source_attempt_id>/.

logical_id.description: Name of the artifact within its attempt (unique per result).

source_job_id.description: The job that produced the artifact.

source_attempt_id.description: The attempt that produced the artifact.
